RIDER + FRAME (FINAL CORRECTION)
Edit this exact transparent 4-column x 2-row eight-frame pixel-art rider-and-bicycle-frame sprite sheet. Preserve the composition, the bike facing RIGHT, four seated pedaling frames in row 1, four out-of-saddle sprint frames in row 2, navy/teal bicycle frame with NO WHEELS, transparent background, and the same adult rider. Keep the frame, axle attachment points, handlebars and crank alignment unchanged. Apply these specific corrections consistently to every appropriate cell:

1. HYGIENE CAP: ALL HAIR MUST BE COMPLETELY TUCKED INSIDE THE WHITE FOOD-SERVICE HYGIENE CAP. Remove every visible brown/black tuft, side hair and especially the dark hair at the back of the head and nape. The cap must enclose the back of the head and all hair, down behind the ears. Retain the pink cap visor, visible face/ear where appropriate, white mask and white arm guards. No exposed hair anywhere in all eight frames.

2. APRON LENGTH: the current pink apron is far too short. Make it a proper long pink kitchen apron with pale edging that reaches JUST ABOVE THE KNEES. In the seated frames, the cloth drapes over the lap and front thighs to just above the kneecaps, with natural bent riding folds. In the sprint frames it also reaches just above the knees and follows the lifted-hip bent-forward posture. Keep loose full-length dark navy trousers and dark shoes. Do not convert the apron into shorts, a tiny waist flap, a skirt, or ankle-length cloth.

3. SMALL WAIST BOW: greatly reduce the enormous pink bow and billowing shapes behind the waist. Replace with one modest compact knot with two small loops and SHORT NARROW ties. No giant ribbons, giant loops, long fluttering fabric flags or huge back flaps in any cell.

4. LEG OCCLUSION: in frame 5 (LOWER LEFT, first sprint frame), the rider's LEFT leg and left foot are on the FAR SIDE of the bicycle and must pass BEHIND the bicycle frame tubes and the near right leg. They must not appear pasted on top of the frame. Keep the near RIGHT leg in front. Apply correct near/far leg overlap in all frames. Hands stay on the bars.

5. HIGH-SPEED COMIC MOTION, LOWER ROW ONLY:
- Legs and feet should read as rapid spinning pedaling, not two perfectly frozen sharply outlined trouser legs. Add controlled semi-transparent dark-navy pixel afterimages and curved/elliptical pedal-motion streaks close around the legs and crank. Partially merge/soften the FAST leg silhouettes and shoe edges so the individual feet are less distinct at racing speed. Retain enough anatomical suggestion to read pedaling, but emphasize circular motion. The four fast cells have successive shifted quarter-turn afterimage phases.
- Add a modest pink/navy fading ghost silhouette trailing LEFT behind the back/hips and rear edge of the torso, with translucent stepped pixel smearing. This is comic speed-induced shape loss, not oversized clothing or ribbon.
- Keep the front face, mask, cap, hands, handlebar, bicycle FRAME and both axle eyelets SHARP. Do not blur the rigid bike frame or change the mounting geometry.
- Retain the short horizontal pale-cyan/ivory speed lines behind the fast rider and blend them with the subtle rear-body afterimage. Effects stay inside each cell; no overlap into neighboring cells.
- Row 1 remains clean, crisp normal pedaling with no speed blur or wind streaks.

Preserve true alpha transparency including fading afterimages. No background, painted checkerboard, labels, typography, road, wheel or ground shadow. Keep the same crisp retro pixel-art visual language; high-speed blur is made of translucent pixel trails rather than a Gaussian blur across the whole image. This is a corrected usable game asset sheet.
